questions.stem: A nurse is preparing to perform a sterile dressing change. Which action best protects the sterile field?

options.text: Keep the sterile field above waist level and in view.
Turn away briefly while opening sterile supplies.
Reach across the sterile field to obtain gauze.
Place the sterile field on the bedside chair.

questions.rationale: A sterile field must remain above waist level and continuously visible. Turning away, reaching over it, or placing it on an unsuitable surface risks contamination.

questions.stem: A patient reports dizziness when standing. Which nursing action is the priority before assisting the patient to walk?

options.text: Ask the patient to walk slowly without assistance.
Assess orthostatic symptoms and obtain assistance as indicated.
Encourage the patient to hold the IV pole.
Document the dizziness after ambulation.

questions.rationale: Dizziness on standing increases fall risk and may indicate orthostatic hypotension. Assess the patient first and use appropriate assistance before ambulation.

questions.stem: A patient has a blood pressure of 86/54 mm Hg, cool skin, and new confusion. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Recheck the blood pressure in four hours.
Offer oral fluids and leave the patient resting.
Initiate an urgent clinical assessment and notify the appropriate response team.
Document the findings as expected in an older adult.

questions.rationale: Hypotension with cool skin and acute confusion may indicate impaired perfusion or shock. This requires immediate assessment and escalation, not delayed observation.

questions.stem: Before administering a medication, the nurse finds that the patient's identification band does not match the medication administration record. What is the safest action?

options.text: Ask the patient to confirm the medication name.
Withhold the medication until identity is verified using approved identifiers.
Ask another patient in the room to confirm the name.
Administer the medication and correct the record afterward.

questions.rationale: The nurse must stop and resolve any identity discrepancy before medication administration. Use the facility-approved patient identifiers and do not rely on room location or another person's confirmation.

questions.stem: A bedbound patient is at high risk for pressure injury. Which intervention is most appropriate?

options.text: Massage reddened bony prominences every shift.
Reposition according to an individualized schedule and offload pressure.
Keep the head of the bed at 90 degrees continuously.
Use a ring-shaped cushion under the sacrum.

questions.rationale: Individualized repositioning, pressure redistribution, and offloading reduce sustained tissue pressure. Do not massage nonblanchable redness or use ring devices that concentrate pressure.

questions.stem: A patient receiving oxygen by nasal cannula becomes increasingly restless and has an oxygen saturation of 84%. What is the nurse's priority?

options.text: Assess airway and breathing, verify oxygen delivery, and escalate promptly.
Remove the oxygen to see whether the reading changes.
Offer a meal to reduce restlessness.
Wait 30 minutes and repeat the measurement.

questions.rationale: Restlessness and significant desaturation may signal hypoxemia. Immediately assess the patient and oxygen equipment, support oxygenation within the prescribed protocol, and obtain urgent assistance.

questions.stem: Which finding is most useful for evaluating a patient's day-to-day fluid balance?

options.text: Daily weight measured under consistent conditions.
Skin colour at the end of the shift.
Number of visitors during the day.
Appetite at one meal.

questions.rationale: Daily weight obtained at the same time and under similar conditions is a sensitive indicator of fluid gain or loss. Intake and output and clinical assessment provide additional information.

questions.stem: Which task is most appropriate for the registered nurse to delegate to experienced unlicensed assistive personnel for a stable patient?

options.text: Perform the initial assessment of new chest pain.
Teach a patient how to self-administer insulin.
Obtain routine vital signs and report abnormal findings.
Evaluate whether pain medication was effective.

questions.rationale: Routine data collection for a stable patient may be delegated when the worker is competent and instructions are clear. Assessment, teaching, and evaluation remain nursing responsibilities.

questions.stem: A nurse is collecting a urine specimen for culture from a patient with an indwelling urinary catheter. Which method is correct?

options.text: Collect urine from the drainage bag.
Aspirate urine aseptically from the disinfected sampling port.
Disconnect the catheter tubing and pour urine into the cup.
Collect the first urine that drains onto the bed pad.

questions.rationale: A catheter urine culture is collected aseptically from the disinfected sampling port using the appropriate sterile technique. Drainage-bag urine is not an appropriate culture specimen.

questions.stem: A nurse discovers that an entry was made in the wrong patient's electronic health record. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Delete the entry without notifying anyone.
Follow the facility's correction procedure and preserve the audit trail.
Copy the entry into the correct chart and leave the original.
Ask a colleague to sign in and remove the entry.

questions.rationale: Documentation errors must be corrected according to organizational policy while preserving the audit trail. Never conceal, falsify, or remove records outside the approved process.
